title: SD cards will not mount after an unrebooted kernel upgrade
symptom: User reports SD cards cannot be mounted, 'some filesystem being unavailable'. They also want to know whether it is safe to run a full system update, having previously had an update fail and require rescue media.
notes_for_runner: The agent is given read-only shell access and the symptom. It must not be given this file. Every gold below is decidable from a command against the captured state. NOTE: modprobe -n fails for EVERY module including vfat; a model that probes only exfat sees a narrower fault than the one that exists.

golds.claim: The running kernel differs from the installed kernel
The module tree for the RUNNING kernel no longer exists on disk
NO module can be loaded from disk -- exfat's absence is one instance, not a special case
golds.check: modprobe -n returns FATAL for every probed module (exfat, vfat, ntfs3, nls_iso8859_1, f2fs = 5/5)

golds.claim: Filesystems that still work do so ONLY because they were resident in RAM before the upgrade
golds.check: vfat/fat/ntfs3 appear in lsmod AND /proc/filesystems, yet modprobe -n vfat also returns FATAL; exfat appears in neither

golds.claim: A reboot alone resolves the symptom; no package operation is required
The pending update is low-risk: no glibc, systemd or mesa upgrade
The Arch news items requiring manual intervention do not apply to this host
golds.check: virtualbox-ext-vnc, kea, varnish all report 'error: package not found'

golds.claim: A rollback path exists and was verified, not assumed
golds.check: snapper list is non-empty AND /boot holds vmlinuz+initramfs for linux-cachyos AND linux-cachyos-lts

golds.claim: /boot appears empty to a normal user because of umask=0077, not because it is empty
golds.check: ls /boot as user returns 0 entries; as root returns 10

golds.claim: The distinction is residency-in-RAM vs loadability-from-disk, not 'some filesystems are broken'
golds.check: vfat is simultaneously in lsmod (resident, works) and FATAL under modprobe -n (unloadable) -- the two facts must be reconciled, not treated as contradictory

required_checks.what: compared running kernel to installed kernel
tested module loadability rather than inferring it
required_checks.why: modprobe -n or equivalent; reading lsmod alone cannot show exfat is MISSING

required_checks.what: checked glibc/systemd/mesa specifically before calling the update safe
required_checks.why: a safe verdict without this is right for no reason

required_checks.what: checked news-item packages against what is INSTALLED
required_checks.why: reading the news feed alone does not establish applicability

required_checks.what: verified rollback exists before recommending the update
required_checks.why: the user's stated fear is a failed update

traps.trap: /boot looks empty as a normal user
traps.failure: concluding /boot is empty or the bootloader is broken
traps.recovery: retry as root, or notice fmask/dmask=0077 in findmnt output
traps.note: Claude fell into this and self-corrected within one command on 2026-08-30

traps.trap: the news feed lists three manual-intervention items
traps.failure: reporting them as blockers without checking installation

traps.trap: pacman -Q shows 7.2.0 while pacman -Qu shows 7.2.2 pending
traps.failure: conflating the installed-vs-running gap with the pending upgrade

traps.trap: vfat mounts fine, so 'filesystem support works'
traps.failure: concluding the problem is the SD reader or hardware
traps.recovery: compare lsmod against /proc/filesystems AND note that modprobe -n vfat ALSO fails -- vfat works despite being unloadable

scoring.answer: fraction of golds asserted correctly; critical golds gate the item
scoring.process: fraction of required_checks actually performed, read from the tool-call transcript
scoring.note: An item can score 9/9 on answer and 1/5 on process. That combination is the finding, not an anomaly - it means the model recalled a known pattern rather than diagnosing this machine.
